advancements.modular_dreams.root.title: Modular Dreams
guide.modular_dreams.book.flow.1: 1. PART BUILDER - shape raw materials into generic parts. All woods make wooden parts; there is no oak or cherry, just wood.
guide.modular_dreams.book.flow.2: 2. ASSEMBLY TABLE - combine a handle, a binding and a head of one tool type into the finished tool.
guide.modular_dreams.book.flow.3: 3. MELTING - copper, iron and gold parts cannot be carved; melt ingots in a furnace with a Melting Upgrade and cast them in molds.
guide.modular_dreams.book.flow.title: The Flow
guide.modular_dreams.book.started.partbu: The PART BUILDER works like a stonecutter: drop a material into the input slot, click the part shape you want from the grid, and take it from the output slot.
Any planks make generic wooden parts; cobblestone makes stone parts. Flint, bone, leather, vine, string, slime and blaze/breeze rods have their own parts.
Each shape costs a few units of material - a pickaxe head takes 3, a binding 2, a shovel head 1.
Metals and diamond cannot be carved: copper, iron, gold and diamond parts must be melted (see the Molds chapter).
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b1: A flint head is cheaper than bone and nearly as fast - great for early tools.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b10: Diamond is in! Diamond parts are melted and cast like the metals. Netherite is NOT a material - it arrives as a tool upgrade in a later update, vanilla-style.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b2: An iron handle multiplies durability by 1.1; a wooden handle adds a small bonus and keeps things cheap.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b3: Blaze rod handles have iron-like handles - useful when wood is scarce, like in the Nether.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b4: Gold parts mine extremely fast but break quickly - pair a gold head with an iron handle to soften the blow.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b5: Terracotta molds last three casts - bake your clay molds before big casting sessions.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b6: Repair your tools with the material of their head: iron ingots for iron, planks for wood.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b7: Parts of the same material stack neatly in chests - generic parts mean fewer item types.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b8: The melting upgrade works while the furnace does other things - keep it fed with ingots.
guide.modular_dreams.book.tips.b9: Modifiers and more trait effects return in a future update - diamond's Hardened trait is already listed, it just needs to awaken.
guide.modular_dreams.intro.1: Why throw away a worn-out tool when you can repair and upgrade it? Modular Dreams lets you build vanilla tools and weapons from generic parts made of vanilla materials.
guide.modular_dreams.intro.2: Keep this book handy - it documents every station, material and part.
guide.modular_dreams.intro.parts.1: Every tool is assembled from exactly three parts - a head, a binding and a handle. There is ONE universal handle and ONE universal binding that fit every tool of their kind, including the sword and the spear; those two simply render with their own special shapes (the sword's binding is called the Guard).
guide.modular_dreams.intro.parts.title: Tool Parts
guide.modular_dreams.intro.philosophy.1: Modular tools cost a little more material than their vanilla counterparts, but they are an investment: repair them forever and re-purpose them with new parts.
guide.modular_dreams.intro.philosophy.2: Stats are inherited from the materials of each part. An iron head mines like iron; a bone handle trades durability for speed. Mix and match to shape the tool you need.
guide.modular_dreams.material.no_head: Binding only - cannot be used as a head.
guide.modular_dreams.materials.intro.1: Head stats are copied from Tinkers' Construct. Handles change durability by a percentage - the diamond handle even boosts mining speed and attack by 10% - and bindings add a small flat bonus.
guide.modular_dreams.materials.intro.2: Materials without head stats (leather, vine, string, slime) are binding-only; blaze and breeze rods are handle-only with iron-like handles.
guide.modular_dreams.materials.title: Materials
guide.modular_dreams.molds.1: Craft a CLAY MOLD from four clay balls and place it on the ground - both molds sit flat like a cutting board.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.2: Right-click the placed CLAY mold with any part to press that shape into the clay. The part is only a template - it is not consumed. Changed your mind? Use a different part on the mold to RE-SHAPE it as often as you like. The mold surface is CUT OUT where the part would sit, leaving a real mold cavity - in the world and on the item. Terracotta molds cannot be shaped by hand: they keep the shape they were baked with.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.3: Break the shaped mold to pick it up, then cook it in a furnace: clay molds become TERRACOTTA molds of the same shape. The terracotta mold is a block too - you can place it down just like the clay one.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.4: A clay mold can be used directly for one casting, but it breaks afterwards. A terracotta mold survives three casts.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.melting.1: Place a MELTING UPGRADE directly UNDERNEATH a furnace, then insert a shaped mold: right-click the upgrade with the mold, or open it (right-click with anything else) and drop the mold into the bottom slot.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.melting.2: Put copper, iron, gold or diamond into the furnace's top slot. With a mold inserted, the metal melts down instead of sitting idle.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.melting.3: Each melted ingot fills the mold: the finished part appears in the MELTING UPGRADE's GUI, in the slot above the mold. The mold loses one use per cast.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.melting.4: Metals and diamond work for every head, binding and handle. Without a mold nothing melts - the ingots simply wait.
guide.modular_dreams.molds.melting.title: The Melting Upgrade
guide.modular_dreams.molds.title: Clay Molds
guide.modular_dreams.started.2.1: The ASSEMBLY TABLE has three input slots in fixed order: HEAD on top, BINDING in the middle, HANDLE at the bottom.
guide.modular_dreams.started.2.2: Place the three parts of one tool type into their slots and the assembled tool appears on the right. The parts stay in the table when you close it.
guide.modular_dreams.started.2.3: The head decides the tool type. The universal handle and the universal binding fit every tool - even a sword or a spear - and each tool just renders its own special part shapes (the sword's binding is the Guard).
guide.modular_dreams.started.2.title: The Assembly Table
guide.modular_dreams.tips.title: Tips & Tricks
guide.modular_dreams.title: Materials & You
guide.modular_dreams.tools.1: Tool durability = (head durability + binding bonus) x handle multiplier + handle bonus, then x the tool's own multiplier.
guide.modular_dreams.tools.2: Mining speed and mining tier come from the head; attack damage comes from the head plus the tool type. A diamond handle multiplies both mining speed and attack damage by 1.1.
guide.modular_dreams.tools.spear.1: The modular spear reaches further than any vanilla weapon - charge the attack to stab from range.
guide.modular_dreams.tools.spear.2: It can also be thrown by holding use, trading the tool itself for a long-range hit.
guide.modular_dreams.tools.spear.title: The Spear
guide.modular_dreams.tools.stats.note: Every assembled tool shows its parts, materials and exact stats in the tooltip.
